decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY covering flexible prototype dimensions and top-or-side connector access.
The existing same-message MODIFY captures vertical installation and connector access but omits the stated flexibility of prototype dimensions.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
so the small board on left is sensors board middle is main and right is power. this is for prototype so I can change dimensions, etc.
the point is that as you can see they stand vertically so if cables are on top it will be easier to connect them or on sides for smaller connectors

value_updates.connector_access: top access preferred, with side access acceptable for smaller connectors

decisions.reason: The general top-or-side access preference does not necessarily replace the battery connector's established back placement, which may remain compatible with an accessible board edge.
The source changes mechanical placement preferences and prototype dimensions, not the sensor connector inventory, types, pinouts, or count.
The electrical interboard topology, connector types, and pinouts remain valid; physical connector placement is represented by the mechanical-layout Requirements.
Board orientation and connector accessibility do not change the I2C speed, pull-ups, cable-length assumptions, or series-resistor configuration.
The source does not change the power-button connector type, target board, signal connection, or control behavior; any physical placement is governed by the main-board mechanical layout.
The source does not alter BOOT/reset behavior, wiring, mounting role, or capacitance.
The mechanical-layout preference does not change the selected ESP32 module.
The source does not change the USB-C programming interface or native USB behavior.
The source does not change the monitored rails, monitoring IC, channel allocation, measurement coverage, or monitor position.
The mechanical prototype and connector-access decision does not change DCDC1 voltage configuration or its regulation objective.
